description: Fixed check of O-implicit-exit-continuation: real three-node implicit removal with transfer interleaved before application acknowledgment, finite TimeoutNow loss, then a deterministic serviced suffix. Compare full captured state over repeated ten-tick periods and independently observe whether the same joint transition remains installed. No-transfer control and ordinary-proposal rescue provide diagnostic context.

harness.description: TestAssuranceJointExitFixed uses public RawNode calls for all mutations and read-only recursive state capture for recurrence. Stops after fixed service periods independently of joint-exit success.
semantic_changes: Crash-free MemoryStorage persistence substitutes external disk, retaining Ready ordering.
Finite deliberate loss of TimeoutNow only in overlap prefix.
Read-only private-state serialization adds observation without changing protocol transitions.

legality.derivation: Three fresh MemoryStorage/RawNode instances Bootstrap the same peer list, process committed bootstrap configuration entries, elect through messages and durably process each Ready before releasing its messages. The implicit remove-3 entry is replicated and applied normally. Only the overlap case invokes TransferLeader(2) after ApplyConfChange but before Advance of that committed batch; calls remain serialized. The interface does not require Advance immediately after ApplyConfChange. One finite window drops only generated TimeoutNow messages; after ten ticks all transport is reliable. All nodes receive one Tick per round and all Ready/network queues are drained between rounds. RawNode has no goroutine or shutdown resource. MemoryStorage substitutes persistence only in a crash-free model; no fake peer acknowledgment, forced commit or direct mutation of protocol state is used.
legality.applicability: Caller-controlled crash-free schedule, no asynchronous storage writes, CheckQuorum enabled. Bootstrap entries are processed before campaigning. All nodes and both quorums remain available.
alternatives: Different legal schedules can complete exit; this check tests the specified overlap, not all configurations.

grounding.derivation: The result reports full state recurrence and live outgoing configuration separately. Recurrence is direct equality of three independently serialized states at ten-tick intervals, including all RawNode fields recursively: local storage, logs, current term/role, membership including live AutoLeave, progress and inflights, timers, queued messages and completion callbacks. The external schedule repeats the same tick order and fair queue-draining loop, with no further drops or client work. Exclusions are logging sinks, MemoryStorage callStats, and its uncontended mutex, which do not influence protocol decisions. RawNode callback function identity is retained; receiver state is separately captured. The source shows random timeout selection only on reset; unchanged role/term and reliable heartbeats keep this suffix outside reset. A recurrent serviced cycle cannot indefinitely retain the admitted implicit joint transition under the automatic-continuation obligation. Control and later-proposal rescue remain diagnostic, not substitute oracles. Status.Config.AutoLeave is not used as live state.
grounding.applicability: The single monitored operation is the overlap case implicit-remove-3. No numeric deadline is inferred. If full recurrence is not observed, the implication alone does not establish or refute eventual completion; retain that scope limitation.
alternatives: Future unrelated proposals or elections can restore progress; neither is owed by the caller in this stable serviced suffix.

observable_properties.description: A fully recurrent, fairly serviced suffix for the admitted implicit transition must not still require the outgoing configuration. Recurrence and active joint state are independently computed from actual target state, not elapsed time.

uncertainties: A nonrecurrent bounded trace alone cannot decide eventual exit.
The recurrence abstraction excludes logging, uncontended mutex state and read-call counters; correspondence review must check those exclusions and random/callback state.
No downstream safety or outage endpoint is observed.
